## Amendments

### 2026-10-20 — `normalisation`

- **From** total_in_degree **to** forward_cone
- Governs: Each edge is divided by the destination's in-degree summed over every relation, counting only the edges whose source the seed can reach, per seed; unsigned row sums over the edges that carry are one. Amendment item 28 as narrowed by decision 9.16.
- Commit `e9758bd07c67`: The per-seed forward-cone divisor is the registered normalisation (decision 9.16)

### 2026-10-22 — `tested_models`

- **From** confirmatory_v2_message_passing_noisy_or and confirmatory_v2_linear_response_noisy_or, each at one-sided 0.025 **to** confirmatory_v2_linear_response_noisy_or
- Governs: One model: the noisy-OR configuration of the linear-response encoder. The sigmoid head was dropped on 15 October 2026 because only noisy-OR has modules that can be read as pathways; the message-passing encoder moved to robustness_models on 22 October 2026 (the owner: "Defer it to robustness. I don't want it constraining things because this is more about mechanistically identifiably predictive nosology"). The registered reason is that only the linear-response encoder has a closed-form steady state, so only there can the sensitivity of a label to a sign-disputed edge, and hence whether a disputed sign is identifiable at all, be read without a training run. With one tested model the familywise chance of a lucky pass is the level the model is tested at, which is why alpha_one_sided returned to 0.05 in the same session (decision 9.78): the registered familywise 0.05 is unchanged and is now carried by one test rather than split across two.
- Commit `342c62d9b156`: Defer the message-passing encoder to a robustness reading

### 2026-10-22 — `robustness_models`

- **From** no such rule; a robustness reading of an encoder was not registered **to** confirmatory_v2_message_passing_noisy_or
- Governs: Read and reported with their intervals outside the tested family, spending no alpha, as the two permutation readings have since 8 October 2026. The message-passing encoder sits here from 22 October 2026 so a conclusion of the tested model can be checked against a second encoder of a different inductive bias without that check constraining the registered family. A robustness reading that disagrees is reported as a disagreement and cannot withdraw the tested model's result; the corroboration a second tested model would have given is therefore given up, which is the cost the owner accepted.
- Commit `342c62d9b156`: Defer the message-passing encoder to a robustness reading

### 2026-10-22 — `alpha_one_sided`

- **From** 0.025 **to** 0.05
- Governs: The tested model is a candidate at one-sided 0.05: H1 first, then its second-stage family by Holm at the same level, so the smaller of H2 and P1 faces 0.025 and the larger faces 0.05. Holm over eight hypotheses was withdrawn on 8 October 2026. The level was halved to 0.025 while two models were tested, where the union bound over two uncorrected tests put the familywise chance of a lucky pass at 2 x 0.025 = 0.05. With tested_models holding one model from 22 October 2026 there is no across-model multiplicity left, the familywise level is this level itself, and the halving no longer buys anything, so it was returned to 0.05 (the owner, 22 October 2026: "Move it back to the .05 alpha please with just one model now"; decision 9.78). This is the more permissive of the two readings of the same registered familywise 0.05 and it was taken before any lockbox was drawn.
- Commit `8174d182d580`: Return the one-sided level to 0.05 now that one model is tested
